root_and_ghu.definition: 1.1.20 includes four dā-type roots and two dhā-type roots and expressly excludes the cutting and purifying dāp/daip teachings. The two positive roots chosen here are the juhotyādi entries cited together in 8.4.17.
root_and_ghu.dhā: ḍudhāñ in holding and nourishing, 03.0011; Kṣīrasvāmin records giving/holding. The Mādhavīya and Dhātupradīpa attribute an additional giving sense to some teachers.

voice_policy: For these ñ-marked agentive roots, A is licensed when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent (1.3.72); the remainder takes P (1.3.78). An isolated translation such as give or place does not settle that condition.

rule_interactions.reduplication: Ślu and 6.1.10 yield the characteristic initial da. Dhā retains contrast in dadhāti and in the word-initial aspiration of dhatte.
rule_interactions.imperatives: 6.4.119 yields dehi and dhehi with loss of the copy. In a blessing 7.1.35 gives optional tāt, which shares its spelling between second and third singular.
rule_interactions.aspiration: 8.2.38 accounts for dh in the specified dhā environments; Kṣīrasvāmin illustrates dhattaḥ and dhatsva.
